# Query packs

<!-- Generated by `python -m AI.query_packs docs --lang en docs/query-packs.en.md`; edit the TOML files in AI/query_packs/packs. -->

[Русская версия](query-packs.md)

A pack is a set of ready queries of one domain for a typical metric source. Applying it adds the queries
to the "Queries" section of the chosen area and fills the SLA references. Latencies of load tools are
converted to milliseconds, node CPU to percent, the CPU of a service instance to a fraction 0..1.

"Verified on `docker/dev-stack`" means that every required query of the pack returned data on
`docker/dev-stack` with live exporters. The other packs are checked for syntax and for the contract of
series and units; run them with the "Check" button before use.

## Bundles

| Bundle | Packs |
|---|---|
| Spring Boot on Kubernetes + k6 (InfluxDB) | `lt-k6-influxql`, `jvm-micrometer`, `http-micrometer`, `db-hikaricp`, `db-postgres-exporter`, `kafka-exporter`, `node-exporter`, `k8s-nodes`, `k8s-workload-health` |
| Spring Boot on virtual machines + JMeter | `lt-jmeter-influxql`, `jvm-micrometer`, `http-micrometer`, `db-hikaricp`, `db-postgres-exporter`, `node-exporter` |
| Java with JMX exporter + Gatling | `lt-gatling-influxql`, `jvm-jmx-exporter`, `http-otel`, `kafka-broker-jmx`, `node-exporter` |
| Go on Kubernetes + k6 (Prometheus remote write) | `lt-k6-prometheus-rw`, `runtime-go`, `http-go`, `db-postgres-exporter`, `node-exporter`, `k8s-nodes`, `k8s-workload-health` |
| Python (FastAPI) on Kubernetes + k6 (Prometheus remote write) | `lt-k6-prometheus-rw`, `k8s-workload-cpu`, `http-python-fastapi`, `db-postgres-exporter`, `node-exporter`, `k8s-nodes`, `k8s-workload-health` |

## Load tool

### Gatling Graphite → InfluxDB (InfluxQL)

`lt-gatling-influxql` v1 · domain "Load testing tool" · InfluxQL

Gatling Graphite output (data.writers = [graphite]) in InfluxDB 1.x with the graphite template `gatling.*.*.*.* measurement.simulation.request.status.field`. Requests then land in the gatling measurement with the simulation, request (allRequests is the summary) and status (ok/ko/all) tags, and users in the rows request="users", status="allUsers" with the active field. count is requests per writePeriod (gatling.data.graphite.writePeriod, 1 s by default). Times are in ms.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `measurement` | `gatling` | Measurement |
| `simulation` | `.*` | Simulation (regular expression). Simulation name in lower case as Gatling writes it. All simulations by default |
| `write_period_sec` | `1` | Write period, s |
| `load_model` | `open` | Load model of the scenario. open — constantUsersPerSec, rampUsersPerSec; closed — constantConcurrentUsers, rampConcurrentUsers. Choices: open, closed |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| LT (Gatling): RPS total | Total test RPS (required) | per second | performance query |
| LT (Gatling): RPS by request | RPS by request | per second |  |
| LT (Gatling): p95(ms) total | p95 response time, whole test | ms | p95 |
| LT (Gatling): p99(ms) total | p99 response time, whole test | ms | p99 |
| LT (Gatling): p95(ms) by request | p95 response time by request | ms |  |
| LT (Gatling): mean response time(ms) | Average response time, whole test (required) | ms | mean latency (forecast) |
| LT (Gatling): error rate (%) | Error rate, whole test | % | error rate |
| LT (Gatling): errors per second by request | Errors per second by request | per second |  |
| LT (Gatling): active users | Virtual users | count | VUs (forecast) |

### Gatling Graphite → VictoriaMetrics (PromQL)

`lt-gatling-graphite-victoriametrics` v1 · domain "Load testing tool" · PromQL · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

Gatling Graphite output (gatling.data.writers = [graphite]) in VictoriaMetrics with Graphite ingestion (-graphiteListenAddr=:2003). VictoriaMetrics stores the whole Graphite path as the metric name: gatling.<simulation>.allRequests.<ok|ko|all>.<count|mean|percentiles95|…> is the summary, gatling.<simulation>.<group>.<request>.<status>.<metric> are the requests (spaces in names become "_"), gatling.<simulation>.users.allUsers.active is the users. Series are selected by __name__, the request name is taken from the path with label_replace. The source is VictoriaMetrics as Prometheus (http://victoria:8428, for a cluster vmselect …/select/0/prometheus) or a Grafana data source of the Prometheus/VictoriaMetrics type. count is requests per writePeriod (1 s by default), times are in ms. By default VictoriaMetrics hides the last 30 s (-search.latencyOffset): build the report of a test that has just finished a minute later.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `root_prefix` | `gatling` | Root prefix. gatling.data.graphite.rootPathPrefix from gatling.conf. A prefix with dots is not supported |
| `simulation` | `[^.]+` | Simulation (regular expression). Simulation name in lower case as Gatling writes it, for example checkoutsimulation. Any by default |
| `window_sec` | `30` | Averaging window, s. Counters are summed and latencies averaged over this window. It must be no shorter than the write period |
| `write_period_sec` | `1` | Write period, s. gatling.data.graphite.writePeriod |
| `load_model` | `open` | Load model of the scenario. open — constantUsersPerSec, rampUsersPerSec; closed — constantConcurrentUsers, rampConcurrentUsers. Choices: open, closed |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| LT (Gatling VM): RPS total | Total test RPS (required) | per second | performance query |
| LT (Gatling VM): RPS by request | RPS by request | per second |  |
| LT (Gatling VM): p95(ms) total | p95 response time, whole test | ms | p95 |
| LT (Gatling VM): p99(ms) total | p99 response time, whole test | ms | p99 |
| LT (Gatling VM): p95(ms) by request | p95 response time by request | ms |  |
| LT (Gatling VM): mean response time(ms) | Average response time, whole test (required) | ms | mean latency (forecast) |
| LT (Gatling VM): error rate (%) | Error rate, whole test | % | error rate |
| LT (Gatling VM): errors per second by request | Errors per second by request | per second |  |
| LT (Gatling VM): active users | Virtual users | count | VUs (forecast) |

### Gatling Graphite → VictoriaMetrics with relabeling (PromQL)

`lt-gatling-graphite-victoriametrics-labels` v1 · domain "Load testing tool" · PromQL · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

Gatling Graphite output in VictoriaMetrics where relabeling rules (-relabelConfig, action: graphite) turn paths into series with labels: gatling.<simulation>.<request>.<status>.<metric> → gatling_request_<metric>{simulation, request, status}, gatling.<simulation>.users.<scenario>.<metric> → gatling_users_<metric>{simulation, request}. The rules are in docs/load-tests.md. Users are also read from gatling_request_active{request="users"}: they land there when the users rule did not fire. Requests inside Gatling groups show up per request only with a rule for six-part paths. If VictoriaMetrics stores whole paths, use the "Gatling Graphite → VictoriaMetrics (PromQL)" pack. count is requests per writePeriod (1 s by default), times are in ms. By default VictoriaMetrics hides the last 30 s (-search.latencyOffset): build the report of a test that has just finished a minute later.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `simulation` | `.+` | Simulation (regular expression). Value of the simulation label: the simulation name in lower case, for example checkoutsimulation. Any by default |
| `window_sec` | `30` | Averaging window, s. Counters are summed and latencies averaged over this window. It must be no shorter than the write period (writePeriod) |
| `load_model` | `open` | Load model of the scenario. open — constantUsersPerSec, rampUsersPerSec; closed — constantConcurrentUsers, rampConcurrentUsers. Choices: open, closed |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| LT (Gatling VM labels): RPS total | Total test RPS (required) | per second | performance query |
| LT (Gatling VM labels): RPS by request | RPS by request | per second |  |
| LT (Gatling VM labels): p95(ms) total | p95 response time, whole test | ms | p95 |
| LT (Gatling VM labels): p99(ms) total | p99 response time, whole test | ms | p99 |
| LT (Gatling VM labels): p95(ms) by request | p95 response time by request | ms |  |
| LT (Gatling VM labels): mean response time(ms) | Average response time, whole test (required) | ms | mean latency (forecast) |
| LT (Gatling VM labels): error rate (%) | Error rate, whole test | % | error rate |
| LT (Gatling VM labels): errors per second by request | Errors per second by request | per second |  |
| LT (Gatling VM labels): active users | Virtual users | count | VUs (forecast) |

### JMeter Backend Listener → InfluxDB (InfluxQL)

`lt-jmeter-influxql` v2 · domain "Load testing tool" · InfluxQL

The built-in JMeter InfluxdbBackendListenerClient: measurement jmeter, tags application, transaction, statut; fields count, countError, avg, pct95.0, pct99.0, maxAT. Rows with transaction="all" are the summary of all samplers, transaction="internal" are the threads. RPS = count per send interval divided by its length. JMeter computes percentiles over a sliding window of samples (backend_metrics_window); values are in ms.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `measurement` | `jmeter` | Measurement |
| `application` | `.*` | Application (regular expression). Value of the application field in the Backend Listener. All applications by default |
| `send_interval_sec` | `5` | Send interval, s. How often the Backend Listener writes points (5 s by default) |
| `load_model` | `closed` | Load model of the scenario. Thread Group — closed; Arrivals/Free-Form Arrivals Thread Group — open. Choices: open, closed |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| LT (JMeter): RPS total | Total test RPS (required) | per second | performance query |
| LT (JMeter): RPS by transaction | RPS by request | per second |  |
| LT (JMeter): p95(ms) total | p95 response time, whole test | ms | p95 |
| LT (JMeter): p99(ms) total | p99 response time, whole test | ms | p99 |
| LT (JMeter): p95(ms) by transaction | p95 response time by request | ms |  |
| LT (JMeter): mean response time(ms) | Average response time, whole test (required) | ms | mean latency (forecast) |
| LT (JMeter): error rate (%) | Error rate, whole test | % | error rate |
| LT (JMeter): errors per second by transaction | Errors per second by request | per second |  |
| LT (JMeter): active threads | Virtual users | count | VUs (forecast) |
| LT (JMeter): RPS by LoadLens instance | RPS by instance of a LoadLens run | per second |  |

### k6 → InfluxDB 1.x (InfluxQL)

`lt-k6-influxql` v3 · domain "Load testing tool" · InfluxQL · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

The built-in k6 output `--out influxdb=http://influxdb:8086/k6`. Latencies are converted to milliseconds (the unit of the SLA thresholds). The overall p95, p99, average and error share are computed over the report resampling interval, RPS per second. The lt_framework domain needs an InfluxQL data source with the k6 database.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `testid` | `.*` | testid tag (regular expression). Value of the testid tag k6 was started with (--tag testid=...). All runs by default; runs started from LoadLens set their own tag |
| `load_model` | `open` | Load model of the scenario. open — executors constant/ramping-arrival-rate, closed — ramping-vus, constant-vus, per-vu-iterations. Choices: open, closed |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| LT (InfluxQL): RPS by group & name | RPS by request | per second |  |
| LT (InfluxQL): checks per second by group & check | Checks per second | per second |  |
| LT (InfluxQL): http_req_duration p95(ms) by group & name | p95 response time by request | ms |  |
| LT (InfluxQL): RPS sum by all groups | Total test RPS (required) | per second | performance query |
| LT (InfluxQL): http_req_duration p95(ms) total | p95 response time, whole test | ms | p95 |
| LT (InfluxQL): http_req_duration p99(ms) total | p99 response time, whole test | ms | p99 |
| LT (InfluxQL): http_req_duration mean(ms) | Average response time, whole test (required) | ms | mean latency (forecast) |
| LT (InfluxQL): error rate (%) | Error rate, whole test | % | error rate |
| LT (InfluxQL): failed requests per second by group & name | Errors per second by request | per second |  |
| LT (InfluxQL): VUs | Virtual users | count | VUs (forecast) |
| LT (InfluxQL): RPS by LoadLens instance | RPS by instance of a LoadLens run | per second |  |

### k6 → InfluxDB 2.x (Flux)

`lt-k6-influx2-flux` v1 · domain "Load testing tool" · Flux · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

The xk6-output-influxdb extension (`--out xk6-influxdb`) writes the same measurements as the built-in k6 output: http_reqs, http_req_duration, http_req_failed, vus. The bucket is set in the binding of the lt_framework domain; LoadLens fills the {bucket}, {start} and {end} placeholders. Latencies are in milliseconds.

| `load_model` | `open` | Load model of the scenario. open — executors constant/ramping-arrival-rate, closed — ramping-vus, constant-vus, per-vu-iterations. Choices: open, closed |

| LT (Flux): RPS by name | RPS by request | per second |  |

| LT (Flux): http_req_duration p99(ms) total | p99 response time, whole test | ms | p99 |
| LT (Flux): http_req_duration p95(ms) by name | p95 response time by request | ms |  |
| LT (Flux): http_req_duration mean(ms) | Average response time, whole test (required) | ms | mean latency (forecast) |

### k6 → Prometheus remote write (native histograms)

`lt-k6-prometheus-native` v2 · domain "Load testing tool" · PromQL · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

k6 output `--out experimental-prometheus-rw` with K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_AS_NATIVE_HISTOGRAM=true. Percentiles and the average are computed over the rate() window, so they are more accurate than trend stats. Needs Prometheus 2.40+ with native histograms enabled (--enable-feature=native-histograms).

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `matchers` | empty | Extra matchers. For example testid="checkout-2025-01-15". Empty means all k6 metrics |
| `window` | `1m` | rate() window |
| `load_model` | `open` | Load model of the scenario. open — executors constant/ramping-arrival-rate, closed — ramping-vus, constant-vus, per-vu-iterations. Choices: open, closed |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| LT (k6 native): RPS total | Total test RPS (required) | per second | performance query |
| LT (k6 native): RPS by name | RPS by request | per second |  |
| LT (k6 native): http_req_duration p95(ms) total | p95 response time, whole test | ms | p95 |
| LT (k6 native): http_req_duration p99(ms) total | p99 response time, whole test | ms | p99 |
| LT (k6 native): http_req_duration p95(ms) by name | p95 response time by request | ms |  |
| LT (k6 native): http_req_duration mean(ms) | Average response time, whole test (required) | ms | mean latency (forecast) |
| LT (k6 native): error rate (%) | Error rate, whole test | % | error rate |
| LT (k6 native): VUs | Virtual users | count | VUs (forecast) |
| LT (k6 native): checks passed (%) by check | Share of successful checks | % |  |
| LT (k6 native): RPS by LoadLens instance | RPS by instance of a LoadLens run | per second |  |

### k6 → Prometheus remote write (trend stats)

`lt-k6-prometheus-rw` v2 · domain "Load testing tool" · PromQL · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

k6 output `--out experimental-prometheus-rw` with trend stats: set K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_STATS="p(95),p(99),avg". k6 computes the trend stats itself, so the overall p95 is the worst p95 among the series. For accurate percentiles over windows use the native histograms pack. To tell the run apart from other tests, add a testid matcher and start k6 with --tag testid=...

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `matchers` | empty | Extra matchers. For example testid="checkout-2025-01-15". Empty means all k6 metrics |
| `window` | `1m` | rate() window |
| `load_model` | `open` | Load model of the scenario. open — executors constant/ramping-arrival-rate, closed — ramping-vus, constant-vus, per-vu-iterations. Choices: open, closed |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| LT (k6 Prometheus): RPS total | Total test RPS (required) | per second | performance query |
| LT (k6 Prometheus): RPS by name | RPS by request | per second |  |
| LT (k6 Prometheus): http_req_duration p95(ms) worst | p95 response time, whole test | ms | p95 |
| LT (k6 Prometheus): http_req_duration p99(ms) worst | p99 response time, whole test | ms | p99 |
| LT (k6 Prometheus): http_req_duration p95(ms) by name | p95 response time by request | ms |  |
| LT (k6 Prometheus): http_req_duration mean(ms) | Average response time, whole test (required) | ms | mean latency (forecast) |
| LT (k6 Prometheus): error rate (%) | Error rate, whole test | % | error rate |
| LT (k6 Prometheus): VUs | Virtual users | count | VUs (forecast) |
| LT (k6 Prometheus): checks passed (%) by check | Share of successful checks | % |  |
| LT (k6 Prometheus): RPS by LoadLens instance | RPS by instance of a LoadLens run | per second |  |

### Locust → Prometheus (locust_exporter)

`lt-locust-prometheus` v1 · domain "Load testing tool" · PromQL · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

Metrics of ContainerSolutions/locust_exporter, which polls the Locust web UI: current RPS and errors by request (the name="Aggregated" row is the summary), p95 of the current window and users. Locust computes the average response time from the start of the test, so it lags behind the steps. Latencies are in milliseconds.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `matchers` | empty | Extra matchers |
| `load_model` | `closed` | Load model of the scenario. Locust users are a closed model; constant_throughput / constant_pacing are closer to an open one. Choices: open, closed |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| LT (Locust): RPS total | Total test RPS (required) | per second | performance query |
| LT (Locust): RPS by name | RPS by request | per second |  |
| LT (Locust): response time p95(ms) current | p95 response time, whole test | ms | p95 |
| LT (Locust): average response time(ms) since start | Average response time, whole test (required) | ms | mean latency (forecast) |
| LT (Locust): error rate (%) | Error rate, whole test | % | error rate |
| LT (Locust): failures per second by name | Errors per second by request | per second |  |
| LT (Locust): users | Virtual users | count | VUs (forecast) |

### Yandex.Tank → InfluxDB (InfluxQL)

`lt-yandex-tank-influxql` v1 · domain "Load testing tool" · InfluxQL

The Yandex.Tank InfluxUploader plugin: measurement overall_meta (fields RPS, active_threads) and overall_quantiles (fields q50…q100 in ms), the label tag (__OVERALL__ is the summary, the others are request labels with labeled: true), the uuid tag is the test id. The uploader does not write the average response time, so the SLA reference for the capacity forecast stays empty. Verify the field names with the "Check" button.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `prefix` | empty | Measurement prefix. The prefix_measurement parameter of the InfluxUploader plugin; empty by default |
| `uuid` | `.*` | Test UUID (regular expression) |
| `load_model` | `open` | Load model of the scenario. An rps schedule (line, const, step) is open; instances in pandora are closed. Choices: open, closed |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| LT (Yandex.Tank): RPS total | Total test RPS (required) | per second | performance query |
| LT (Yandex.Tank): RPS by label | RPS by request | per second |  |
| LT (Yandex.Tank): p95(ms) total | p95 response time, whole test | ms | p95 |
| LT (Yandex.Tank): p99(ms) total | p99 response time, whole test | ms | p99 |
| LT (Yandex.Tank): p95(ms) by label | p95 response time by request | ms |  |
| LT (Yandex.Tank): active threads | Virtual users | count | VUs (forecast) |

## Application runtime

### Go runtime: client_golang

`runtime-go` v1 · domain "JVM and runtime" · PromQL · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

Standard client_golang collectors: go_* and process_*. The series go to the "JVM" domain with the "Go runtime" prefix because the resource plan takes service CPU from there. Process CPU comes in cores: set the container CPU limit (or GOMAXPROCS) to get a 0..1 fraction. In Kubernetes the "Containers: CPU and memory against the limit" pack is more accurate.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `service_label` | `job` | Label with the service name |
| `matchers` | empty | Extra matchers |
| `cpu_limit_cores` | `1` | Cores per instance. Container CPU limit or GOMAXPROCS: process CPU is divided by this number |
| `window` | `2m` | rate() window |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Go runtime: CPU (share of limit) by (job, instance) | Service instance CPU (required) | fraction 0..1 | service CPU (resource plan) |
| Go runtime: heap alloc (bytes) by (job, instance) | Used heap (required) | bytes |  |
| Go runtime: resident memory (bytes) by (job, instance) | Process resident memory | bytes |  |
| Go runtime: goroutines by (job, instance) | Goroutines | count |  |
| Go runtime: GC pause avg (s) by (job, instance) | Average GC pause | s |  |
| Go runtime: GC cycles per second by (job, instance) | Garbage collections per second | per second |  |
| Go runtime: allocation rate (bytes/s) by (job, instance) | Allocation rate | bytes/s |  |
| Go runtime: OS threads by (job, instance) | Threads | count |  |
| Go runtime: open file descriptors by (job, instance) | Open file descriptors | count |  |

### JVM: Micrometer (Spring Boot Actuator, Quarkus)

`jvm-micrometer` v1 · domain "JVM and runtime" · PromQL · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

JVM metrics from Micrometer: /actuator/prometheus in Spring Boot or /q/metrics in Quarkus. The service name comes from the common Micrometer tag (management.metrics.tags.application). process_cpu_usage is the share of all CPUs available to the process (in a container JDK 11+ takes the limit into account), so it fits the resource plan.

|---|---|---|
| `service_label` | `application` | Label with the service name |
| `matchers` | empty | Extra matchers. For example namespace="shop". Empty means every service with the service label |
| `window` | `2m` | rate() window |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |

| JVM: Heap max (bytes) by (application, instance) | Maximum heap | bytes |  |
| JVM: Process CPU usage by (application, instance) | Service instance CPU (required) | fraction 0..1 | service CPU (resource plan) |
| JVM: Live data after GC (bytes) by (application, instance) | Live data after GC | bytes |  |
| JVM: GC pause time (%) by (application, instance) | Share of time in GC pauses | % |  |
| JVM: GC pause avg (s) by (application, instance) | Average GC pause | s |  |
| JVM: GC pauses per second by (application, instance) | Garbage collections per second | per second |  |
| JVM: Live threads by (application, instance) | Threads | count |  |

### JVM: Prometheus JMX exporter, client_java

`jvm-jmx-exporter` v1 · domain "JVM and runtime" · PromQL

### Python runtime: prometheus_client

`runtime-python` v1 · domain "JVM and runtime" · PromQL · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

Standard prometheus_client collectors: process_* and python_gc_*. The series go to the "JVM" domain with the "Python runtime" prefix because the resource plan takes service CPU from there. Process CPU comes in cores. In multiprocess mode (gunicorn with PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR) there are no process_* metrics; then take CPU and memory from the "Containers: CPU and memory against the limit" pack.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `service_label` | `job` | Label with the service name |
| `matchers` | empty | Extra matchers |
| `cpu_limit_cores` | `1` | Cores per instance. Usually 1 for a single Python process: the GIL does not let it use more than one core |
| `window` | `2m` | rate() window |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Python runtime: CPU (share of limit) by (job, instance) | Service instance CPU (required) | fraction 0..1 | service CPU (resource plan) |
| Python runtime: resident memory (bytes) by (job, instance) | Process resident memory (required) | bytes |  |
| Python runtime: GC collections per second by (job, instance, generation) | Garbage collections per second | per second |  |
| Python runtime: GC objects collected per second by (job, instance) | Objects collected by GC per second | per second |  |
| Python runtime: open file descriptors by (job, instance) | Open file descriptors | count |  |

### Containers: CPU and memory against the limit (cAdvisor + kube-state-metrics)

`k8s-workload-cpu` v1 · domain "JVM and runtime" · PromQL

Container CPU and memory for a service in any language: cAdvisor (kubelet) and limits from kube-state-metrics 2.x. The service is the container name, the instance is the pod. CPU is a fraction of the container limit, so it fits the resource plan; containers without a CPU limit are left out of the series. The series go to the "JVM" domain.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `namespace` | `.+` | Namespace (regular expression) |
| `container` | `.+` | Container (regular expression). Limit it to the services of the test, for example orders\|payments |
| `ksm_matchers` | `job=~".*kube-state-metrics.*"` | kube-state-metrics matchers |
| `window` | `2m` | rate() window |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Containers: CPU usage (share of limit) by (application, instance) | Service instance CPU (required) | fraction 0..1 | service CPU (resource plan) |
| Containers: memory working set (bytes) by (application, instance) | Process resident memory | bytes |  |
| Containers: memory limit (bytes) by (application, instance) | Container memory limit | bytes |  |

### Kafka brokers: JMX exporter / Strimzi

`kafka-broker-jmx` v1 · domain "Kafka" · PromQL

Broker metrics from the JMX exporter with the Strimzi rules (kafka-metrics.yaml) or the kafka-2_0_0.yml example: kafka_server_*, kafka_controller_*, kafka_network_*. The names depend on the exporter rules: check the queries with the "Check" button and deselect the ones that return nothing.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `broker_label` | `instance` | Broker label. In Strimzi pod is more convenient |
| `matchers` | empty | Extra matchers. For example strimzi_io_cluster="my-cluster" |
| `window` | `2m` | rate() window |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kafka brokers: messages in per second by topic | Incoming messages per second (required) | per second |  |
| Kafka brokers: bytes in per second by broker | Broker incoming traffic | bytes/s |  |
| Kafka brokers: bytes out per second by broker | Broker outgoing traffic | bytes/s |  |
| Kafka brokers: under-replicated partitions by broker | Under-replicated partitions (required) | count |  |
| Kafka brokers: offline partitions | Partitions without a leader | count |  |
| Kafka brokers: Produce p99 total time (ms) by broker | p99 of Produce handling on the broker | ms |  |
| Kafka brokers: network processor idle (%) by broker | Idle time of broker network threads | % |  |
| Kafka brokers: connections by broker | Broker connections | count |  |

### Kafka clients: Micrometer (Spring Kafka)

`kafka-client-micrometer` v1 · domain "Kafka" · PromQL

Kafka client metrics from Micrometer KafkaClientMetrics (Spring Boot enables them for Spring Kafka factories): consumer lag, read and write rate, producer errors and latency, listener time.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `service_label` | `application` | Label with the service name |
| `matchers` | empty | Extra matchers |
| `window` | `2m` | rate() window |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kafka clients: max consumer lag (records) by application | Maximum client lag (required) | count |  |
| Kafka clients: consumed records per second by application | Messages read per second | per second |  |
| Kafka clients: sent records per second by application | Records sent per second | per second |  |
| Kafka clients: producer errors per second by application | Send errors per second | per second |  |
| Kafka clients: producer request latency avg (ms) by application | Average producer request latency | ms |  |
| Kafka clients: listener processing avg (sec) by application | Average listener handling time | s |  |

### Kafka: kafka_exporter (danielqsj)

`kafka-exporter` v1 · domain "Kafka" · PromQL · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

kafka_exporter metrics: consumer group lag, topic write rate from partition offsets, group members and under-replicated partitions. Internal topics (__consumer_offsets and the like) are excluded.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `matchers` | empty | Extra matchers. For example topic=~"orders.*" |
| `window` | `2m` | rate() window |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kafka: consumergroup lag by topic & group | Consumer group lag (required) | count |  |
| Kafka: messages in per second by topic | Incoming messages per second | per second |  |
| Kafka: consumed messages per second by topic & group | Messages read per second | per second |  |
| Kafka: consumer group members by group | Consumer group members | count |  |
| Kafka: under-replicated partitions by topic | Under-replicated partitions | count |  |
| Kafka: brokers | Brokers in the cluster | count |  |

## Nodes and Kubernetes

### Kubernetes: workload health (restarts, throttling, replicas, OOM)

`k8s-workload-health` v1 · domain "Node resources" · PromQL

Signals that explain degradation under load in Kubernetes: container restarts, CPU throttling by the CFS quota, memory against the limit, OOMKilled, available and desired deployment replicas and HPA replicas. Sources: cAdvisor (kubelet) and kube-state-metrics 2.x. Limit it to the namespace of the test environment.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `namespace` | `.+` | Namespace (regular expression) |
| `ksm_matchers` | `job=~".*kube-state-metrics.*"` | kube-state-metrics matchers |
| `window` | `2m` | rate() window |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| K8s workloads: container restarts (per 5m) by namespace & pod | Container restarts (required) | count |  |
| K8s workloads: CPU throttling (%) by namespace & pod (top 20) | CPU throttling | % |  |
| K8s workloads: memory working set (% of limit) by namespace & pod (top 20) | Memory, % of the limit | % |  |
| K8s workloads: OOMKilled containers by namespace & pod | Containers killed by OOM | count |  |
| K8s workloads: available replicas by namespace & deployment | Available replicas | count |  |
| K8s workloads: desired replicas by namespace & deployment | Desired replicas | count |  |
| K8s workloads: HPA current replicas by namespace & hpa | HPA replicas | count |  |

### Kubernetes: nodes (kube-state-metrics)

`k8s-nodes` v1 · domain "Node resources" · PromQL

Node state from kube-state-metrics 2.x: readiness, CPU and memory requests against allocatable (how densely pods are scheduled) and the number of pods. The actual CPU and memory load of the nodes comes from the node_exporter pack; install them together.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ksm_matchers` | `job=~".*kube-state-metrics.*"` | kube-state-metrics matchers |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| K8s nodes: Ready by node | Node in the Ready state | count |  |
| K8s nodes: CPU requests (% of allocatable) by node | CPU requests, % of allocatable (required) | % |  |
| K8s nodes: Memory requests (% of allocatable) by node | Memory requests, % of allocatable | % |  |
| K8s nodes: Pods by node | Pods on the node | count |  |

### Load generators: node_exporter

`lt-generators-node-exporter` v1 · domain "Load generator resources" · PromQL · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

Resources of the machines that run the load testing tool: CPU, memory, load per core, network and TCP connections from node_exporter on the generators. With them the report sees whether a generator hit a resource limit and whether the applied load and latencies can be trusted. Limit the matchers to the generator hosts, not the system under test.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `matchers` | `job=~".*loadgen.*"` | Generator matchers. Generator hosts only, for example job="loadgen" or instance=~"10.0.5.*" |
| `window` | `1m` | rate() window |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generators: CPU usage (%) by host | Load generator CPU (required) | % |  |
| Generators: Memory usage (%) by host | Load generator memory (required) | % |  |
| Generators: load1 per core by host | Generator load1 per core | ratio |  |
| Generators: Network receive (bytes/s) by host | Generator network: receive | bytes/s |  |
| Generators: Network transmit (bytes/s) by host | Generator network: transmit | bytes/s |  |
| Generators: TCP established by host | Generator TCP connections | count |  |

### Windows nodes: windows_exporter

`windows-exporter` v1 · domain "Node resources" · PromQL

Windows server resources from prometheus-community/windows_exporter (collectors cpu, cs, os, memory, logical_disk, net, system): CPU and memory in percent (the source of the CPU and memory SLA), processor queue per core, disk utilization and fill, network. Works with the names before and after 0.30 (memory from cs/os or memory). A node is named by the instance address without the port.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `matchers` | empty | Extra matchers. For example job="windows" |
| `window` | `2m` | rate() window |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows nodes: CPU usage (%) by node | Node CPU (required) | % | node CPU |
| Windows nodes: Memory usage (%) by node | Node memory (required) | % | node memory |
| Windows nodes: processor queue per core by node | load1 per core | ratio |  |
| Windows nodes: Disk utilization of the busiest volume (%) by node | Disk utilization | % |  |
| Windows nodes: Network receive (bytes/s) by node | Network: receive | bytes/s |  |
| Windows nodes: Network transmit (bytes/s) by node | Network: transmit | bytes/s |  |
| Windows nodes: Disk used (%) by node | File system fill | % |  |

### Nodes: node_exporter (VM and Kubernetes)

`node-exporter` v1 · domain "Node resources" · PromQL · verified on `docker/dev-stack`

Node resources from node_exporter: CPU and memory in percent (the source of the CPU and memory SLA and of the resource plan), load per core, disk utilization, network, file system fill. A node is named by the hostname from node_uname_info: the node name in Kubernetes, the host name on a VM.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `matchers` | `job=~".*node.*"` | node_exporter matchers. Limit it to the nodes of the test environment, for example job="node-exporter", instance=~"10.0.1.*" |
| `window` | `2m` | rate() window |

| Query | Role | Unit | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nodes: CPU usage (%) by node | Node CPU (required) | % | node CPU |
| Nodes: Memory usage (%) by node | Node memory (required) | % | node memory |
| Nodes: load1 per core by node | load1 per core | ratio |  |
| Nodes: Disk utilization of the busiest device (%) by node | Disk utilization | % |  |
| Nodes: Network receive (bytes/s) by node | Network: receive | bytes/s |  |
| Nodes: Network transmit (bytes/s) by node | Network: transmit | bytes/s |  |
| Nodes: Filesystem used (%) by node | File system fill | % |  |
